name: MugenCodex Chapter Coins Paywall
author: mugencodex

sections.description:
MugenCodex Chapter Coins Paywall is a lightweight coin-based access plugin for chapters, episodes, web novels, comics and serialized WordPress content.

Lock premium content, give readers coins manually and let logged-in users permanently unlock chapters from their accounts. It works without memberships, subscriptions, payment gateways or a heavy ecommerce setup.

Main features:

  • Lock unlimited posts, pages and supported public custom post types.
  • Set the coin cost for each locked item.
  • Show a configurable preview before the lock box.
  • Let logged-in readers unlock content with their coin balance.
  • Manage user coin balances from inside the plugin.
  • Grant manual access to one or more users and chapters.
  • Lock several items through WordPress Bulk Edit.
  • Lock matching content by tag.
  • Filter users and review coin and unlock activity logs.
  • Use shortcodes for wallet and unlocked-content pages.

This plugin uses a manual coin workflow. It does not process payments or sell coins automatically.

Shortcodes:

  • [content_coins_wallet]
  • [content_coins_purchases]
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin ZIP from Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate MugenCodex Chapter Coins Paywall.
  3. Open Chapter Coins > Settings and set the default coin rules.
  4. Lock a post, page or chapter from the editor, Bulk Edit, or by tag.
  5. Open Chapter Coins > Users and add coins to a reader.
  6. Test the unlock flow with a normal user account.
sections.faq:
Can readers buy coins automatically?

No. This plugin uses manual coin balances. The site administrator adds or removes coins.

Is there a chapter limit?

No. You can lock any number of posts, pages and supported public custom post types.

Can one coin equal one chapter?

Yes. Set the default cost to 1 coin. Individual content can use a different cost.

Does access stay saved?

Yes. When a reader unlocks content, access is saved to the WordPress user account.

Can I lock custom post types?

Yes, when the custom post type is public and uses normal WordPress content.

Does the plugin send data to external services?

No. Coin balances, access records and plugin settings are stored in the site’s own WordPress database.
